summary_en: IQ-JEPA pretrains a joint-embedding predictive encoder on unlabeled complex ultrasound IQ data and fine-tunes it for quantitative sound-speed reconstruction. Its Hermitian vision transformer is designed around the phase structure of pulse-echo measurements. The paper reports roughly threefold label-efficiency improvement at 10,000 labels and shows frozen features containing both sound-speed and attenuation information. It is a strong core acoustic-imaging candidate, but should remain in candidates until a peer-reviewed venue is verified.

summary_en: A two-stage robotic-ultrasound framework in which a latent conditional diffusion model predicts future ultrasound observations from recent frames and commanded probe motion, and a goal-conditioned transformer learns probe trajectories using rewards from the frozen world model. It is relevant because it explicitly models ultrasound image formation under contact and view changes, but the primary contribution is robotic acquisition control rather than acoustic reconstruction, so candidate status is appropriate.
